item.title: US-led Gaza peace board warns Hamas over kites after Israeli threat
item.description: The US-led board overseeing the Gaza peace plan warned Hamas on Tuesday to halt militant activity, including flying kites, after Israel threatened retaliatory strikes. A Board of Peace official said Israel must also respect the ceasefire, limiting military action to responses to “genuine and imminent threats.”

item.title: Despite ceasefire, Israeli strikes still kill in Gaza and the West Bank
item.description: Despite a ceasefire that has been in place since October 2025, violence continues in Gaza. On August 23, Israeli strikes left several people dead in the enclave, and a young boy was killed by the Israeli military in the West Bank, according to local authorities. Since the announcement of the truce, more than 1,280 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza, while Israel has reported the launch of drones, balloons and kites towards its territory.

item.title: Israel warns of 'forceful' response to kites flown from Gaza
item.description: Hamas says the kites found in Israeli border communities in recent days were launched by children in Gaza.

item.title: Israel's Netanyahu says Iran tried to assassinate one of his sons
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Monday that Iran had attempted to assassinate one of his two sons, without providing evidence or further details. “Iran tried to kill one of my sons,” Netanyahu told Israel’s Channel 14, as he discussed security arrangements ahead of the October 27 election.

item.title: What to Know About Bank Melli, Singled Out in U.S. Call for Economic War
item.description: Bank Melli, Iran’s largest lender, already faces waves of sanctions that severely limit its ability to operate abroad. Every foreign branch must be shut down, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.

item.title: Trump calls leaders to isolate Iran. And, SCOTUS backs Trump for now on mail-in voting
item.description: President Trump is calling on world leaders to join his economic war against Iran. And, the Supreme Court is backing the president for now on his order to restrict mail-in voting.

item.title: France and Saudi Arabia hold talks ranging from Middle East to esports
item.description: Mohammed bin Salman has arrived in Paris for a two-day official visit with French President Emmanuel Macron. Talks are expected to include the war in Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, as well as new energy routes to bypass the Strait. The two made an appearance at the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup, held for the first time outside of Saudi Arabia but largely funded by Riyadh.

item.title: Trump Administration to Return Diplomats to Middle East Embassies
item.description: Evacuated foreign service officers could begin heading back to their posts as early as this week, an internal document shows, suggesting Washington does not anticipate a renewal of full-scale conflict with Iran.

item.title: Iran tried to assassinate one of Netanyahu's sons, prime minister says
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu claims Iran tried to murder one of his sons, urging enhanced protection for prime ministerial candidates during the election campaign.

item.title: שר ההגנה הישראלי שם לב לכוח נאט"ו כאשר המתיחות במזרח התיכון גוברת: "הרפתקאות מסוכנות"
item.description: שר ההגנה הישראלי, ישראל כץ, הזהיר את רג'פ טאיפ ארדואן שלא לבחון את נחישותה של ישראל לאחר התקיפה של בסיס אבו אל-דוחור בסוריה.
